subject: music
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The Baroque period is generally dated from around 1600 to approximately which year?
questions.explain: The Baroque era is conventionally dated c.1600-1750, ending around the death of J.S. Bach.

questions.q: In a Baroque concerto grosso, what is the name given to the small group of solo instruments?
questions.explain: The concertino is the small solo group, contrasted with the ripieno (the full ensemble).

questions.q: The basso continuo of the Baroque period was most commonly realised by which pairing of instruments?
questions.explain: A chordal instrument such as harpsichord plus a bass instrument such as cello together provided the continuous bass and harmony.

questions.q: What are the three main sections of Classical sonata form, in order?
questions.explain: Sonata form presents themes (exposition), transforms them (development) and restates them (recapitulation).

questions.q: What is an 'Alberti bass'?
questions.explain: An Alberti bass is a left-hand accompaniment of broken chords, common in Classical keyboard music.

questions.q: What best describes 'programme music' from the Romantic period?
options: Instrumental music that tells a story or depicts a scene
Music written only for church worship
Music that has no fixed key or metre
Music composed for a solo unaccompanied voice
questions.explain: Programme music is instrumental music designed to portray a narrative, mood or image.

questions.q: In film music, what is a 'leitmotif'?
options: A recurring theme linked to a character, place or idea
The main title heard over the opening credits
A sudden loud chord used to shock the audience
Music that a character sings on screen
questions.explain: A leitmotif is a short recurring musical idea associated with a particular character, place or concept.

questions.q: Which of the following is an example of non-diegetic sound in a film?
options: Orchestral background score the characters cannot hear
A song playing from a radio on screen
Footsteps made by an actor walking
questions.explain: Non-diegetic sound is added for the audience only and does not exist within the world of the characters.

questions.q: Which film score was composed by John Williams?
options: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
questions.explain: John Williams composed Star Wars; the other scores are by Morricone, Horner and Zimmer respectively.

questions.q: In a cartoon, the music precisely matches each of a character's footsteps and mimics an object falling. This technique is known as:
questions.explain: Mickey-mousing is when the music is closely synchronised with the on-screen action.

questions.q: The bodhrán, used in Irish traditional music, is what kind of instrument?
questions.explain: The bodhrán is a shallow frame drum, usually struck with a double-ended beater called a tipper.

questions.q: How are the uilleann pipes supplied with air?
options: By a bellows worked with the player's arm
By the player blowing through a mouthpiece
questions.explain: The uilleann pipes are bellows-blown, distinguishing them from mouth-blown bagpipes.

questions.q: In which time signature is an Irish jig typically written?
questions.explain: The jig is a compound-time dance, most commonly in 6/8.

questions.q: What is 'sean-nós' in the Irish tradition?
options: An unaccompanied, highly ornamented solo song
A fast instrumental group dance tune
questions.explain: Sean-nós ('old style') is unaccompanied, ornamented solo singing, traditionally in the Irish language.

questions.q: You hear an Irish dance tune in simple 4/4, played very fast in a smooth flow of even quavers. Which dance is it most likely to be?
questions.explain: The reel is a fast dance in simple duple/quadruple time with a steady, even quaver movement.

questions.q: Which device produces programmed electronic percussion patterns, widely used in popular music since the 1980s?
questions.explain: A drum machine generates and sequences electronic drum sounds and rhythms.

questions.q: A 'backbeat', common in pop and rock, places emphasis on which beats of a 4/4 bar?
questions.explain: The backbeat stresses the normally weaker beats 2 and 4, typically on the snare drum.

questions.q: The short, catchy and memorable part of a pop song designed to grab the listener is usually called the:
questions.explain: A hook is a memorable musical or lyrical idea meant to catch and hold the listener's attention.

questions.q: A producer takes a short section of an existing recording and reuses it within a new track. This technique is called:
questions.explain: Sampling reuses a portion of a pre-existing recording within a new piece of music.

questions.q: You hear a small solo group alternating with the full string orchestra throughout a Baroque work. This is characteristic of which genre?
questions.explain: The concerto grosso contrasts a small concertino group with the full ripieno ensemble.

specSource: CCEA GCSE Music (2017) specification; Component 3: Listening and Appraising
